name: Yucca

facts.what: Flower petals and flower stalk; fruit of some species
facts.how: Petals raw or cooked; stalk roasted young
facts.value: Modest calories; the petals are the easy food

caution: Eat the petals (remove the bitter green centers) and only the young stalk before it hardens. Roots are not food. Confirm you have a yucca, not a look-alike agave. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: A rosette of stiff sword-leaves sending up a tall spike of creamy bell flowers. Unlike agave, the leaves are not toothed along the edge.

sections.title: Uses
sections.body: The crunchy petals go raw into salads or blanched into dishes; the tender young flower stalk can be roasted like a vegetable.
